children: Apple Inc. (AAPL, Financials), the maker of the iPhone and other consumer tech products, has finally thrown its hat into the ring over foldable phones. Now it needs to clarify who the $1,999 device is really for.

The new iPhone Duo can run work, entertainment and creative apps across its larger foldable display, and Apple is also promoting it as a personal AI hub. But analysts at the event noted the posture looked unusually vast.
That's important, because that top storage option costs $3,199, which is a lot more than you'd spend on a standard premium smartphone. Foldables are still a niche market, too.

IDC forecasts them to account for less than 3% of worldwide smartphone sales in 2026 and sees little change next year. The launch may still work initially because Apple may have enough committed customers.

Counterpoint expects the business may sell about 6 million handsets by the end of the year, potentially giving Apple almost a quarter of the worldwide foldable market. Samsung presently has about 40% market share in the category.

Initial demand will be less important for investors than what occurs once the initial hype has worn off. Apple's challenge is to prove that the Duo can be more than a style accessory for the rich early-adopter crowd. The next test will be if sales remain robust as pent-up demand from existing iPhone owners starts to dry up.

title: Apple Launches $1,999 Foldable iPhone Duo, but Analysts Question Its Mass-Market Appeal
